edition.sessionCovered: Tue, Nov 24 close (Gold -2.5% to $3,560 as dollar resumes advance — 11th decline in 12 sessions · silver -4.7% to $41 hits 12-month low · Brent +1.8% to $91 on IRGC Hormuz mines — 4 tankers catch fire · WTI $82 · Goldman raises Dec Brent to $105, warns $140 · copper -4.8% to $5.38/lb erasing Monday's rally · platinum -5.6% · Nasdaq 100 -2%, S&P -0.5%, Dow +0.9% to 50,040, Nvidia -6% · BTC $60,459 · corn +15¢ to 450¼¢ · Nov 27 deadline 2 days · US expands Iran sanctions, deploys 3rd carrier · VP Vance meets Qatar PM · Oct PCE due Wed · Thanksgiving Thu · OPEC+ Nov 29)
edition.fomc: Next: 9–10 Dec (25bp hike ~90%; Oct PCE due Wed Nov 25; Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26; policy rate 3.75–4.00%)
edition.stripNote: Tue 24 Nov. Tuesday's session reversed Monday's risk-on impulse across nearly every asset class. The dollar resumed its advance as hawkish Fed rhetoric returned, with the dollar index approaching 19-month highs. COMEX gold settled 2.47% lower at $3,559.90 — the eleventh decline in twelve sessions — erasing much of Monday's 3.9% rebound. Spot gold closed near $3,560 per ounce. Silver plunged approximately 4.7% to $41, hitting a 12-month low. Platinum fell 5.6% to $1,256; palladium lost $900 at $870. Oil diverged sharply: Brent crude rallied 1.8% to approximately $91 per barrel after IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires aboard all four vessels. WTI rose to $82. Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent crude forecast to $105 per barrel and warned of a $140 risk scenario if Hormuz traffic disruptions worsen. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group to the Gulf; Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister. LME base metals erased Monday's Nvidia-driven gains: copper fell 4.8% to $5.38 per pound ($11,858 per tonne), tin dropped 3.5% to $39,650, nickel fell 2% to $15,100, and zinc eased 1.7% to $3,440. US equities gave back part of Monday's surge — the Nasdaq 100 fell 2%, the S&P 500 dropped 0.5%, and Nvidia fell 6% — though the Dow rose 0.9% to close at 50,040 on defensive rotation. The November 27 gallium/germanium/antimony deadline is now 2 days away with no extension announced. December corn rose approximately 15 cents to 450¼ cents; December SRW wheat gained 11 cents to 588¾ cents; January soybeans edged up to 1,232 cents. Bitcoin slipped 1.2% to $60,459; Ethereum fell to $1,703. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 11 (Extreme Fear). LNG JKM eased to $29 per MMBtu from $31. The October PCE inflation report is due Wednesday; markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving; OPEC+ meets November 29.

overview: Tuesday's session reversed Monday's risk-on impulse across nearly every asset class. The dollar resumed its advance, sending gold down 2.5% to $3,560 — the eleventh decline in twelve sessions — and silver to a 12-month low near $41. COMEX gold settled at $3,559.90. LME base metals erased Monday's Nvidia-driven gains: copper fell 4.8% to $5.38 per pound ($11,858 per tonne), tin dropped 3.5% to $39,650, nickel fell 2% to $15,100, and zinc eased 1.7% to $3,440. Platinum plunged 5.6% to $1,256; palladium lost $900 again at $870. Oil diverged sharply from the broader risk-off tone: Brent rallied 1.8% to approximately $91 per barrel after IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires aboard all four vessels. WTI rose to $82. Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent forecast to $105 and warned of a $140 risk scenario if Hormuz traffic disruptions worsen. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group. US equities gave back a portion of Monday's rally — the Nasdaq 100 fell 2%, the S&P 500 dropped 0.5%, and Nvidia fell 6% — though the Dow rose 0.9% to close at 50,040 on defensive rotation. Bitcoin slipped to $60,459; Ethereum to $1,703.

The November 27 deadline for China's export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony is now 2 days away with no extension announced — no major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday. Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss regional stability and potential de-escalation of the Hormuz crisis. OPEC+ ministers meet November 29 to decide 2027 output policy amid a tightening supply backdrop — Brent rallied on the mine attacks despite Libyan supply returning, complicating the group's calculus. The October PCE inflation report due Wednesday is the next data point for December rate-hike expectations, currently priced at approximately 90% for a 25bp increase. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving. Grains rallied on the session: corn rose approximately 15 cents to 450¼ cents per bushel, wheat gained 11 cents to 588¾ cents, and soybeans edged up to 1,232 cents — the dollar strength notwithstanding, export demand and Black Sea disruption supported buying. LNG JKM eased to $29 per MMBtu from $31 as near-term demand paused; the structural supply deficit from Hormuz remains. Newcastle coal eased 2% to $147. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 11 (Extreme Fear).

watchItems.title: IRGC mines strike four tankers in Hormuz — Brent rallies to $91, Goldman raises Dec forecast to $105 and warns of $140
watchItems.text: IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, causing fires aboard all four vessels. Brent crude rallied 1.8% to approximately $91 per barrel — diverging sharply from the broader risk-off session. Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent crude forecast to $105 per barrel and warned of a $140 risk scenario if Hormuz traffic disruptions worsen. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group to the Gulf. Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss regional stability and potential de-escalation. Combined Hormuz traffic remains approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels. Three US carrier strike groups are now in the Gulf. OPEC+ ministers meet November 29 to decide 2027 output policy amid the tightening supply backdrop.

watchItems.title: November 27 gallium, germanium and antimony deadline now 2 days away — no extension, no diplomatic venue remains
watchItems.text: The November 27 deadline for China's US-specific export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony is now 2 days away with no extension announced. No major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday over fossil fuel phase-out wording. Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China versus approximately $460 domestically — a roughly 4.5x premium. The deadline arrives as the broader critical minerals complex faces additional pressure from renewed dollar strength and risk-off sentiment. Alcoa's Wagerup gallium refinery has taken FID but is not yet producing. If the bans resume on Thursday, Western semiconductor and defence supply chains face renewed disruption. China produces approximately 99% of global gallium and 60–80% of germanium.

watchItems.title: LME base metals erase Monday's Nvidia rally as dollar resumes advance — copper -4.8%, platinum -5.6%, silver at 12-month low
watchItems.text: Tuesday's session erased Monday's Nvidia-driven gains across the entire base and precious metals complex. Copper fell 4.8% to $5.38 per pound ($11,858 per tonne LME), giving back Monday's 2.4% recovery. Platinum plunged 5.6% to $1,256. Tin dropped 3.5% to $39,650. Nickel fell 2% to $15,100. Silver hit a 12-month low at $41. Gold settled at $3,560 — the eleventh decline in twelve sessions. The common driver was the dollar resuming its advance after Monday's brief retreat on the Nvidia rally. The pattern highlights the fragility of risk-on impulses in the current rate-hiking cycle: without sustained equity follow-through, the dollar quickly reasserts dominance over metals.

watchItems.title: October PCE due Wednesday — Thanksgiving Thursday — OPEC+ meets Saturday November 29
watchItems.text: The October PCE inflation report due Wednesday is the next swing factor for December rate-hike expectations, currently priced at approximately 90% for a 25bp increase at the December 9–10 FOMC meeting. A hot print would reinforce the dollar rally that has driven gold to multi-month lows and pressured base metals. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, creating a compressed trading window. OPEC+ ministers meet Saturday November 29 to decide 2027 output policy — the meeting takes on added significance after Goldman Sachs raised its Brent forecast to $105 and warned of $140 on further Hormuz disruption. The juxtaposition is notable: oil is rallying on supply fears while nearly every other commodity is falling on demand fears driven by dollar strength.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: COMEX settle $3,559.90 -2.47% · 11th decline in 12 sessions · dollar resumed advance · Monday's 3.9% rebound erased · Oct PCE due Wed
desk.sum: Gold fell sharply on Tuesday, with COMEX December futures settling 2.47% lower at $3,559.90 — the eleventh decline in twelve sessions — erasing much of Monday's 3.9% rebound. Spot gold closed near $3,560 per ounce. The dollar resumed its advance after Monday's brief retreat, with the dollar index approaching 19-month highs. The proximate driver was renewed hawkish Fed rhetoric and the absence of equity follow-through — the Nasdaq 100 fell 2% and Nvidia dropped 6%, removing the risk-on impulse that had briefly supported gold on Monday. The pattern underscores the fragility of counter-trend rallies during a sustained rate-hiking cycle. The October PCE inflation report due Wednesday is the next swing factor for December rate-hike expectations, currently priced at approximately 90% for a 25bp hike. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving. Key support at $3,500; resistance at $3,600.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: Hit 12-month low · gold-silver ratio widened to ~87 · dollar strength resumes · higher beta amplified losses · Oct PCE due Wed
desk.sum: Silver plunged approximately 4.7% to $41 per ounce on Tuesday, hitting a 12-month low as the dollar resumed its advance from 19-month highs. Silver's higher beta to gold amplified the downside — Monday's 3.6% rebound was entirely erased and then some. The gold-silver ratio widened to approximately 87 as silver's industrial exposure left it more vulnerable to the risk-off shift. The decline took silver below the $42 support level that had been reclaimed just the previous session. The Nvidia-driven equity rally failed to sustain, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 2% and removing the risk-on impulse. The October PCE due Wednesday is the next key data point. Key support at $40; resistance at $43.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $82 · IRGC mines struck 4 tankers in Hormuz — fires aboard all 4 · Goldman raises Dec forecast to $105, warns $140 · US expands Iran sanctions, deploys 3rd carrier · VP Vance meets Qatar PM · OPEC+ Nov 29
desk.sum: Brent crude rallied 1.8% to approximately $91 per barrel on Tuesday — diverging sharply from the broader risk-off session — after IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires aboard all four vessels. WTI rose to $82. Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent crude forecast to $105 per barrel and warned of a $140 risk scenario if Hormuz traffic disruptions worsen. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group to the Gulf. Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss regional stability. The oil rally despite falling equities and strengthening dollar underscores how supply-side geopolitical risk now dominates crude sentiment. OPEC+ ministers meet November 29 to decide 2027 output policy.
desk.src: Reuters · Trading Economics · Goldman Sachs · Kotak Neo

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME $11,858/t · erased Monday's 2.4% rally and then some · dollar resumed advance · Yangshan premium record $360 · macro headwinds dominate
desk.sum: Copper fell 4.8% to $5.38 per pound ($11,858 per tonne LME) on Tuesday, erasing Monday's 2.4% recovery and extending to a fresh multi-week low as the dollar resumed its advance. The sell-off was driven by the same dollar strength that pressured the entire base metals complex — the Nvidia-driven risk-on impulse proved to be a one-day event. The Yangshan import premium remains at a record $360 per tonne, and Chinese physical demand is robust, but macro headwinds from rate-hike expectations and dollar strength dominate near-term pricing. Copper is now approximately 20% below its September record of $14,875 per tonne. Key support at $5.25/lb ($11,575/t).

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Eased from $150 · risk-off weighed despite winter demand · LNG supply crisis intact · Brent rally to $91 mixed signal · still up ~38% YTD · OPEC+ Nov 29
desk.sum: Newcastle coal eased approximately 2% to $147 per tonne on Tuesday, breaking from the $150 level it had held for several sessions. The decline came as the broader risk-off mood and weaker industrial commodity sentiment weighed, despite winter demand and the ongoing LNG supply crisis providing structural support. Coal remains up approximately 38% year to date. The Brent crude rally to $91 on the Hormuz mine attacks provides a mixed signal — higher oil prices support coal-to-gas substitution economics, but the broader risk aversion that accompanies geopolitical escalation weighs on industrial demand expectations. QatarEnergy's force majeure continues through at least end-December 2026.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Monday's 2.7% rebound fully erased · dollar strength resumes · sharp reversal · South African supply still constrained · session's worst performer
desk.sum: Platinum plunged 5.6% to approximately $1,256 per ounce on Tuesday — the session's worst-performing major commodity — as the dollar resumed its advance and Monday's 2.7% rebound was fully erased. The sell-off took platinum to its lowest level since late 2024. The move highlights the metal's vulnerability in a risk-off environment: its thin market amplifies both rallies and declines. South African mine supply remains constrained by ongoing power issues, and hydrogen electrolysis demand provides structural long-term support, but near-term macro headwinds dominate. Key support at $1,220; resistance at $1,295.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Lost $900 again · EV transition headwind dominant · dollar strength resumes · down ~38% YoY · structurally challenged
desk.sum: Palladium fell 3.3% to approximately $870 per ounce on Tuesday, losing the psychologically significant $900 level it had just reclaimed the previous session. The decline was driven by the dollar resuming its advance and the broader risk-off shift. Palladium's structural headwind from the EV transition — battery EVs require no catalytic converter — continues to cap any attempted rallies. Down approximately 38% year-over-year. The pattern of reclaiming $900 and immediately losing it reflects the metal's fundamental weakness. Key support at $850; resistance at $900.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: IRGC mines struck 4 tankers — fires aboard all 4 · Brent rallies to $91 · Goldman: $105 Dec forecast, $140 risk · US expands sanctions, deploys 3rd carrier · VP Vance meets Qatar PM · JMIC: SEVERE · traffic 65% below pre-conflict · 3 carriers in Gulf
desk.sum: IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, causing fires aboard all four vessels — a significant escalation in the attack methodology. Brent crude rallied 1.8% to $91 on the news. Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent forecast to $105 and warned of a $140 risk scenario if traffic disruptions worsen. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group to the Gulf. Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss regional stability and potential de-escalation. JMIC continues to rate the threat as severe with further deliberate attacks highly likely. Combined Hormuz traffic remains approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels. OPEC+ ministers meet November 29.
desk.src: CNN · gCaptain · UKMTO · JMIC · Reuters · Goldman Sachs

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: Dec front-month · up ~15¢ · fund short-covering · export demand · Black Sea disruption supports · dollar strength limited upside
desk.sum: December corn rallied approximately 15 cents to 450¼ cents per bushel on Tuesday, the session's best-performing commodity. The move appeared driven by fund short-covering and export demand, with Black Sea maritime disruption continuing to support US competitiveness. The rally came despite renewed dollar strength, suggesting the buying had a fundamental basis rather than relying on currency tailwinds. US corn export commitments remain below year-ago levels but have been improving. South American planting continues under generally favourable conditions. Key resistance at 455 cents; support at 440 cents.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: Dec SRW · up 11¢ · fund short-covering alongside corn · Black Sea disruption ongoing · 2 days to Nov 27 deadline
desk.sum: December SRW wheat gained 11 cents to 588¾ cents per bushel on Tuesday, rallying alongside corn as fund short-covering lifted the grain complex. The gains came despite renewed dollar strength. Black Sea maritime disruption continues to affect grain export routes, supporting US wheat competitiveness. SovEcon's Russian wheat export estimate of 36 million tonnes — below the USDA forecast — provides structural support. The November 27 deadline for gallium, germanium and antimony, now 2 days away, adds to the broader geopolitical uncertainty. Key resistance at 595 cents; support at 580 cents.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: January front-month ~$12.32 · up 3¼¢ · meal support continued · export demand solid · South American competition
desk.sum: January soybeans edged up 3¼ cents to 1,232 cents per bushel on Tuesday, modestly higher as soybean meal strength continued to provide support. The gain was more muted than corn and wheat, reflecting the bean market's more balanced supply-demand picture. US soybean export commitments remain up approximately 80% year-over-year — the strongest among the grain complex. South American supplies remain competitive at current exchange rates. The dollar strength that pressured metals had less impact on grains, which are more driven by physical demand flows. Key support at 1,220 cents.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $1,703 · gave back Monday's Nvidia-driven spike · Fear & Greed 11 (Extreme Fear) · Nasdaq 100 -2% weighed · Dec hike odds ~90%
desk.sum: Bitcoin slipped 1.2% to $60,459 on Tuesday, giving back a portion of Monday's Nvidia-driven intraday spike to $63,888. Ethereum fell to approximately $1,703. The decline tracked the broader equity retreat — the Nasdaq 100 fell 2% and Nvidia dropped 6% — confirming that Monday's crypto bounce was a sympathy trade rather than a sustained reversal. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 11 (Extreme Fear). Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows have now exceeded $1 billion for three consecutive weeks. The key test remains whether Bitcoin can hold above $60,000 as equities attempt to stabilise. The October PCE due Wednesday could add further pressure if inflation runs hot.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM Dec contract eased from $31 · TTF ~$28 · HH ~$3.15 · QatarEnergy FM continues · Hormuz mine attacks add supply risk · EU storage ~71% · Brent rally to $91 complicates LNG economics
desk.sum: The Asian LNG spot JKM December contract eased to $29 per MMBtu from $31, pulling back as near-term demand paused ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. TTF sits near $28 per MMBtu; Henry Hub near $3.15. The structural supply deficit from Hormuz-related disruption remains intact, however, and Tuesday's mine attacks on four tankers added further supply-side uncertainty. EU gas storage at approximately 71% is roughly 20% below the five-year average heading into winter. QatarEnergy's force majeure extends through at least end-December 2026. The Brent crude rally to $91 complicates LNG pricing economics by raising the oil-linked component of some supply contracts.
desk.src: S&P Global Platts · Global LNG Hub · Trading Economics

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait ~$765 · Hormuz mine attacks add further supply risk · 2 days to Nov 27 deadline · Brent rally to $91 · 3 US carriers in Gulf
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated at approximately $1,200 per tonne CFR Southeast Asia. Tuesday's IRGC mine attacks on four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz add further supply-side risk to Middle Eastern sulfur logistics. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). The Brent crude rally to $91 supports the petroleum-sulfur production dynamic. The November 27 export-control deadline is 2 days away with no extension announced. The United States expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group, while Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss de-escalation.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · grain rally supportive · Brent rally raises input costs slightly · Black Sea disruption adds logistics risk
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds at approximately $358 per tonne. BPC's India contract remains approximately $25 above China's 2026 benchmark at $383 per tonne CFR. Tuesday's grain rally — corn up 15 cents, wheat up 11 cents — is supportive for fertiliser demand sentiment. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. The Brent crude rally to $91 on Hormuz mine attacks modestly raises potash production input costs. Black Sea disruption continues to add logistics risk to potash trade routes from the region.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: 2 days to Nov 27 deadline · Rotterdam $18,300–19,000/t · prices stabilised after Oct sell-off · no extension announced · no diplomatic venue remains
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) holds near ¥92,000 per tonne, having stabilised after the sharp decline from ¥105,000 in early October. Overseas antimony sits at approximately $18,300–19,000 per tonne in Rotterdam. The November 27 deadline is now 2 days away with no extension announced. No major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday. Market participants continue to price in ban resumption. If the deadline passes without extension on Thursday, overseas prices could spike further. China produces close to half of global mined antimony.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: Up >130% since early 2025 · 2 days to Nov 27 deadline · China domestic Ga ~$460/kg · no diplomatic venue remains · ban resumption increasingly priced in
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, with Chinese domestic gallium at approximately $460 per kilogram — a roughly 4.5x premium. The November 27 deadline is now 2 days away with no extension announced. No major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday. China produces approximately 99% of global gallium and 60–80% of germanium. The underlying licensing regimes remain in force during the suspension. Alcoa's Wagerup gallium refinery has taken FID but is not yet producing. Ban resumption is increasingly priced in. If the bans resume on Thursday, Western semiconductor and defence supply chains face renewed disruption.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Steady at $5.30 · upstream tightness · VRFB adoption timeline uncertain · China-Russia-SA control 90%+ · Nov 27 deadline 2 days
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds at approximately $5.30 per pound in Europe, supported by persistent upstream tightness. The November 27 deadline, now 2 days away, affects the broader critical minerals complex. No major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but large-scale adoption timing remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Holding near $5,200 · Ivory Coast mid-crop may fall 42–50% YoY · ICE stocks at 2.5-year high · risk-off may ease speculative buying · $5,000 support intact
desk.sum: ICE cocoa holds near $5,200 per tonne, range-bound as competing forces offset each other. Ivory Coast's Sodexam projects 2026/27 output down 21–25% due to El Niño, and Reuters sources suggest the mid-crop could fall 42–50% year-on-year to 300,000–350,000 tonnes. Against this, ICE warehouse inventories sit at a 2.5-year high of approximately 3.8 million bags. Tuesday's broader risk-off mood may ease speculative buying pressure. The $5,000 level has held as strong psychological support. Chocolate demand remains subdued at current price levels.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: Continued gradual decline · Rotterdam $16–17/lb · DRC logistics disruption ongoing · NMC-to-LFP shift structural headwind · dollar strength negative
desk.sum: Cobalt is estimated near $32,500 per tonne, continuing a gradual decline. Rotterdam standard-grade cobalt metal sits at $16–17 per pound. The DRC bridge collapse continues to have secondary effects on cobalt logistics, with alternative routes adding time and cost. The NMC-to-LFP battery chemistry shift weighs on the structural demand outlook. Tuesday's renewed dollar strength adds further headwind. The market remains in structural surplus.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Continued drift lower · structural oversupply persists · Goldman: 444k t global surplus by 2028 · November destocking continues · dollar strength negative
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate continues to drift lower near ¥88,000 per tonne, extending the decline from ¥90,000 earlier in November. Structural oversupply remains the dominant theme, with Goldman Sachs projecting a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028. SMM data shows sustained monthly destocking in November. The EU's plan to cap Chinese EV imports at 350,000 units per year adds a demand headwind. Supply ramp-ups in Australia and South America continue to outpace demand growth. Tuesday's renewed dollar strength adds further pressure. The ¥85,000 zone represents next major support.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight · fungal blight ongoing · oil rally to $91 raises synthetic rubber costs · auto demand solid
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), range-bound. Southeast Asian supply remains tight, with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Tuesday's oil rally to $91 raises synthetic rubber production costs, tilting the balance toward natural rubber compared to the previous session when oil was at $89.37. Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles. The dollar strength that pressured metals had a more muted impact on rubber.

desk.name: Uranium
desk.m: Spot held near $90 · term price $98/lb near record · IAEA: 78 reactors under construction · miners sliding while prices hold · AI demand structural
desk.sum: Uranium spot holds near $90 per pound U₃O₈, with long-term contract prices at $98 per pound — approaching the $100 milestone. Despite spot prices holding above $90 for most of November, uranium miners (URNM ETF) have continued to slide, reflecting rate sensitivity, contract-price lag and ETF-driven selling. The IAEA counts 78 reactors under construction worldwide. Kazatomprom reported 25% year-on-year sales turnover growth in Q3 with a 17% rise in average realized prices. AI data-centre power demand remains a structural driver. The broader risk-off shift and dollar strength had limited impact on uranium's supply-driven narrative.

desk.name: Rare Earths
desk.m: Pr-Nd prices on the rise per SMM · ex-China NdPr below $110/kg · Nov 27 deadline 2 days · downstream demand sluggish
desk.sum: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide holds at approximately $72 per kilogram domestically in China. SMM reports that Pr-Nd prices are on the rise, with suppliers holding firm and limiting price concessions. Ex-China NdPr prices remain below $110 per kilogram as oversupply builds outside China. The November 27 deadline for gallium, germanium and antimony — now 2 days away — adds uncertainty to the broader critical minerals complex. Downstream magnetic material orders remain sluggish and buyers are cautious about high-priced inventory.

desk.name: Manganese
desk.m: South Africa 37% · Gabon 18% · miners holding firm pricing stance · CIF China flat · risk-off sentiment weighs on steel demand outlook
desk.sum: Manganese ore (44% Mn content) trades near $4.40 per dry metric tonne unit CIF China, flat. Miners continue holding a firm pricing stance. South Africa supplies about 37% of global ore and Gabon 18%. Steel production consumes 90% of manganese demand. Tuesday's broader risk-off mood and equity decline weigh on steel demand sentiment, though the Dow's 0.9% gain on defensive rotation partially offsets. The dollar resuming its advance is modestly negative for dollar-denominated commodity pricing.

desk.name: Nickel
desk.m: LME 3M ~$15,100 · erased Monday's gains · Indonesian RKAB uncertainty · global surplus continues · dollar strength negative
desk.sum: LME nickel fell approximately 2% to $15,100 per tonne on Tuesday, erasing Monday's modest gains as the dollar resumed its advance. Indonesian RKAB mining quota uncertainty persists — potential tightening provides a floor while the global nickel surplus from Indonesian NPI and HPAL expansions caps upside. The broader LME complex was uniformly weaker as Monday's Nvidia-driven risk-on impulse faded. The dollar strength that sent gold and silver sharply lower also pressured nickel. Key support at $15,000.

desk.name: Tin
desk.m: LME 3M ~$39,650 · erased Monday's gains · Myanmar ban constraining supply · LME backwardation wide · dollar strength and risk-off dominate
desk.sum: LME tin fell 3.5% to approximately $39,650 per tonne on Tuesday, erasing Monday's modest recovery as the dollar resumed its advance and risk-off sentiment returned. The decline was sharper than most base metals, reflecting tin's thinner market and sensitivity to macro shifts. Structural supply constraints persist from Myanmar's Wa State mining ban and Indonesian export licensing tightness. The LME backwardation remains wide, signalling tight near-term supply even as prices fall on macro headwinds. The November 27 deadline, now 2 days away, adds geopolitical uncertainty.

desk.name: Zinc
desk.m: LME 3M ~$3,440 · eased from $3,500 · TCs deeply negative · structural deficit intact · dollar strength negative
desk.sum: LME zinc eased 1.7% to approximately $3,440 per tonne on Tuesday, breaking below the $3,500 level it had held as the dollar resumed its advance. Treatment charges remain deeply negative, forcing continued smelter curtailments outside China. The structural supply deficit remains intact despite near-term macro pressure. Zinc is still up approximately 13% year-over-year. India's HZL previously cut zinc and lead benchmarks despite mixed LME trends. Key support at $3,400.

desk.name: Tungsten
desk.m: Rotterdam APT $2,750 · China FOB $1,845 · Western ~3.5x China · 2 days to Nov 27 deadline · no diplomatic venue remains
desk.sum: European tungsten APT holds at $2,750 per mtu in Rotterdam, while Chinese FOB sits at $1,845 per mtu — Western prices remain roughly 3.5 times Chinese domestic levels. The November 27 deadline is now 2 days away with no extension announced. No major multilateral venue remains after COP31 collapsed on Sunday. The market continues to reflect the fragmentation created by China's export controls. If the bans resume on Thursday, the Western premium could widen further.

desk.name: Helium
desk.m: Up 358% YTD · Ras Laffan repair 3–5 years · IRGC mines struck 4 tankers Tue · VP Vance met Qatar PM · exports recovering slowly
desk.sum: Grade-A helium trades near $390 per thousand cubic feet, at critical levels. Tuesday's IRGC mine attacks on four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz add further risk to already-disrupted helium supply logistics from Qatar. QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility repairs remain estimated at 3–5 years. Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss regional stability — de-escalation would benefit helium supply recovery. Qatar and the US together supply about 81% of global helium. Russia's export controls extend through 2027. The November 27 deadline for gallium, germanium and antimony is 2 days away.

desk.name: Phosphate
desk.m: OCP 30% global · DAP $560/t · sulfur cost surge pressuring economics · grain rally supportive for demand
desk.sum: Phosphate rock trades near $120 per tonne FOB Morocco, with Morocco's OCP Group controlling about 30% of global trade. DAP prices sit near $560 per tonne CFR India. The sulfur price surge continues to pressure phosphate production economics. Tuesday's grain rally — corn up 15 cents, wheat up 11 cents — is supportive for fertiliser demand sentiment. The Brent crude rally to $91 on Hormuz mine attacks further reduces the probability of Middle Eastern sulfur supply normalising, keeping the cost structure elevated.

quiz: COMEX gold settled 2.47% lower at $3,559.90 on Tuesday — the eleventh decline in twelve sessions — as the dollar resumed its advance and erased much of Monday's 3.9% rebound from a 14-month low.
Silver surged 4.7% on Tuesday to $45 per ounce, extending Monday's rally as industrial demand from the solar sector accelerated and the gold-silver ratio narrowed to 80.
Silver actually fell approximately 4.7% to $41 per ounce — hitting a 12-month low — as the dollar resumed its advance. The gold-silver ratio widened to approximately 87, not narrowed to 80.
IRGC-deployed naval mines struck four tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, causing fires aboard all four vessels, as Brent crude rallied 1.8% to approximately $91 per barrel.
The Nasdaq 100 rose 2% on Tuesday, extending Monday's tech-led rally, as Nvidia gained another 6% and the Dow advanced 1.5% to close above 51,000.

The Nasdaq 100 actually fell 2% on Tuesday and Nvidia dropped approximately 6%, giving back a portion of Monday's 31% surge. The Dow did rise, but only 0.9% to close at 50,040 — not 1.5% to above 51,000.

Goldman Sachs raised its December 2026 Brent crude forecast to $105 per barrel and warned of a $140 risk scenario if Hormuz traffic disruptions worsen, as the US expanded sanctions on Iran and deployed a third carrier strike group.
LME copper rose 4.8% on Tuesday to $5.95 per pound as Chinese demand accelerated and the dollar continued to retreat from 19-month highs, extending Monday's recovery.
LME copper actually fell approximately 4.8% to $5.38 per pound ($11,858 per tonne) on Tuesday, erasing Monday's 2.4% recovery. The dollar resumed its advance rather than continuing to retreat.

The November 27 deadline for China's export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony is now 2 days away with no extension announced, as Vice President Vance met Qatar's Prime Minister to discuss the broader regional crisis.
Newcastle thermal coal surged 5% on Tuesday to $157 per tonne as the Brent crude rally above $91 per barrel boosted the entire energy complex and winter demand accelerated stockpiling.

Newcastle coal actually eased approximately 2% to $147 per tonne on Tuesday. While Brent crude did rally to $91, coal moved in the opposite direction as risk-off sentiment weighed on industrial commodities.
